semantic_correction.stem: A post-stroke client has confirmed oropharyngeal dysphagia and is cleared for a modified oral diet. Which nursing plan best reduces swallowing-related risk?

options.A: Follow the individualized swallowing plan for positioning, texture, pacing, cueing, and supervision, and reassess if status changes.
options.B: Use the same thickened-liquid level and chin-tuck position for every client with post-stroke dysphagia.
options.C: Encourage rapid eating to finish before fatigue develops even when coughing or repeated swallows occur.
options.D: Stop observing swallowing once a modified diet is ordered because texture changes eliminate aspiration risk.

semantic_correction.rationale: ASHA guidance emphasizes individualized dysphagia management based on swallowing assessment. Management may include posture and positioning, compensatory strategies, bolus or diet-texture modification, pacing or cueing, assistance, and patient/caregiver education. ASHA also states that texture-modified foods and thickened fluids may not eliminate aspiration or pneumonia risk and that reassessment may be needed when functional or medical status changes. The 2026 AHA/ASA stroke guideline likewise emphasizes that swallowing evaluation guides management and that aspiration risk can persist despite screening or oral-intake restrictions. Therefore the nurse should follow the individualized swallowing plan and continue observation and reassessment.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Implement post-stroke dysphagia precautions according to the individualized swallowing plan and continue monitoring because modified diets do not eliminate aspiration risk.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest. The revised item tests individualized swallowing precautions and ongoing monitoring with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It applies assessment-specific swallowing strategies and preserves ongoing observation and reassessment.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Posture and liquid consistency recommendations depend on individual swallowing physiology and assessment findings.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Rapid intake despite coughing, fatigue, or repeated swallows can increase swallowing-related risk.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Texture modification does not eliminate aspiration or pneumonia risk, so observation remains necessary.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone reflects individualized, assessment-based management with continued monitoring.
cueing_check: All four choices are swallowing-management plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
